strengths: Ambitious and meaningful problem formulation: Extending satellite-to-ground generation from single isolated panoramas to continuous, trajectory-controlled video sequences addresses a major challenge with high utility for digital twin modeling, simulation, and autonomous driving.

Well-grounded geometric framework: The integration of a tri-plane scene representation with ray-based deformable attention effectively bridges the extreme viewpoint gap between overhead and ground panoramas without requiring ground-truth 3D meshes or digital elevation models.

Principled and efficient temporal modeling: Incorporating epipolar constraints into the temporal cross-attention restricts candidate matches to geometrically plausible regions along the trajectory, substantially reducing memory complexity from O((NHW)^2) to O(NHW * NM) and improving multi-frame structural coherence.

Valuable benchmark contribution: The creation of VIGOR++, expanding coverage across 10 metropolitan areas with continuous video sequences and trajectory annotations, provides a much-needed benchmark for cross-view video synthesis research.

Thorough evaluation: The paper demonstrates consistent quantitative and qualitative improvements over relevant baselines across multiple datasets (VIGOR++, CVUSA, VIGOR), backed by convincing ablation experiments on temporal attention and downstream cross-view geo-localization.
weaknesses: Underspecified tri-plane initialization: The initialization of the orthogonal vertical planes (XZ and YZ) from a single 2D overhead satellite view is vague in Section 3.1. The manuscript mentions cross-view hybrid attention and projections, but does not clarify how features along the vertical dimension are initially seeded prior to attention updates.

Implementation details of epipolar curve sampling: In 360-degree equirectangular panoramas, epipolar curves form complex non-linear paths rather than straight lines. The paper omits important practical implementation details regarding how candidate points are sampled/discretized along the epipolar curve and the tolerance threshold used to enforce Eq. 6.

Limited evaluation on long-horizon drift: The temporal attention relies on a sparse window attending only to the two preceding frames. While computationally efficient, the paper does not thoroughly explore whether this sliding window leads to cumulative geometric or appearance drift during long trajectories.

Omission of failure modes and dynamic elements: Real-world street-view sequences often feature dynamic objects (e.g., moving vehicles, pedestrians) and challenging occlusions. The paper lacks discussion on failure cases or the behavior of the model when overhead satellite views differ significantly in capture time or lighting from ground-level imagery.

strengths: Addresses an ambitious and practically valuable problem: generating continuous, geometrically coherent street-level panoramic videos from a single satellite image and camera trajectory without relying on auxiliary height maps or multi-view satellite captures.

The geometric modeling is well-motivated: using a tri-plane scene representation initialized from the top-down satellite view, ray-guided deformable sampling to bridge cross-view perspective differences, and epipolar-constrained temporal attention to reduce computation while enforcing multi-view consistency.

Solid empirical results: SatDreamer360 achieves clear quantitative and qualitative advantages over existing baselines (e.g., ControlS2S, Sat2Density, EscherNet) on both video coherence (FVD, CLIPSIM) and image fidelity metrics.

Valuable benchmark contribution: the curated VIGOR++ dataset provides continuous panoramic trajectories across 10 cities, providing a useful resource for future research in cross-view video synthesis and localization.
Comprehensive validation, including single-image cross-view benchmarks (CVUSA, VIGOR), efficiency/memory scaling ablations, and a downstream cross-view camera localization evaluation.
weaknesses: Low output resolution: The generated panoramic sequences are produced at 128 x 512 resolution, which limits visual sharpness and applicability to high-fidelity downstream simulation tasks.

Technical novelty of individual components is somewhat incremental: Tri-plane spatial encoding with Cross-View Hybrid Attention (CVHA) and ray-based deformable attention are largely adaptations from existing 3D perception frameworks (e.g., BEVFormer, TPVFormer), and epipolar-guided attention is an established concept in multi-view geometry.

Formulation details for equipolar geometry on panoramas: While Eq. 6 correctly expresses the epipolar constraint for directional rays, epipolar curves on equirectangular panoramas are non-linear (sinusoidal). The paper does not thoroughly discuss how the discrete point sampling set along these curves is efficiently implemented during U-Net feature attention.

Baseline comparisons for video generation are somewhat constrained: Comparisons are primarily against single-frame models evaluated frame-by-frame (Sat2Density, ControlS2S) and one general multi-view model (EscherNet). Comparing or adapting contemporary trajectory-controlled video diffusion frameworks (e.g., CameraCtrl, MotionCtrl) would provide a stronger benchmark.

strengths: The paper addresses a challenging and practically important problem: synthesizing continuous, geometrically consistent ground-level street-view panoramic videos conditioned on a single satellite image and camera trajectory.

The technical design is sound and well-motivated: combining a tri-plane scene representation with ray-based deformable pixel attention bridges the large perspective gap between satellite and street views without requiring ground-truth height maps.

The epipolar-constrained temporal attention module introduces valuable geometric priors into the temporal attention layers, enforcing multi-frame consistency while reducing computational and memory complexity from quadratic in image tokens to linear along epipolar curves.

The paper introduces VIGOR++, an extensive benchmark with trajectory annotations across 10 cities, and demonstrates consistent quantitative and qualitative improvements over baselines on video metrics (FVD, CLIPSIM) and downstream cross-view localization.
weaknesses: Implementation details regarding the geometry and triplane initialization are somewhat vague: the paper states ResNet features align with the XY plane, but does not clearly explain how the orthogonal XZ and YZ planes are initialized before applying Cross-view Hybrid Attention (CVHA).

Panoramic epipolar geometry nuance: Equation (6) uses standard epipolar constraints, but in equirectangular projection, epipolar lines map to sinusoidal curves on the spherical panorama. The paper lacks a precise explanation of how the candidate matching points along the epipolar curve are discretized and sampled in practice.

Output resolution and sequence length are relatively constrained: the synthesized panorama resolution is 128x512, and the demonstrated sequences appear restricted to short sequences (under 18 frames in Figure 7), limiting immediate real-world deployment.

Baselines for video generation are somewhat limited: the method is compared against single-image cross-view methods (Sat2Density, ControlS2S) applied frame-by-frame and a generic multi-view model (EscherNet). Conditioning modern video diffusion architectures (e.g., SVD or AnimateDiff) on the satellite features would have served as a stronger video baseline.

strengths: Addresses an important and challenging problem: synthesizing continuous, multi-view consistent panoramic ground-level scene sequences from only a single top-down satellite image and camera trajectory.

Well-grounded geometric design: the combination of a satellite-derived triplane representation, ray-guided deformable pixel attention, and equirectangular epipolar-constrained temporal attention effectively bridges the drastic cross-view disparity while enforcing temporal/spatial coherence.
Introduction of the large-scale VIGOR++ benchmark (>90k pairs across 10 cities) with ground trajectories, addressing a clear gap in existing single-frame cross-view datasets.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across single-frame and sequence benchmarks using perceptual, semantic, pixel, and 3D reconstruction consistency metrics (e.g., using Pi3 for 3D evaluation), along with downstream proof-of-concept on cross-view geo-localization.

Thorough ablation studies demonstrating the computational efficiency and performance gains of the triplane over BEV, ray-based deformable attention over full cross-attention, and sparse epipolar attention over dense attention.
weaknesses: The generated panoramic resolution is limited to 128 x 512 (to match legacy single-frame benchmarks), which restricts visual sharpness and fine-grained architectural details compared to modern high-resolution generative models.
As acknowledged in the limitations, trajectory points spaced closer than ~8m tend to yield nearly identical outputs due to training sampling sparsity (15–20m) and triplane grid resolution.
The discretization details for sampling points along the epipolar curves on equirectangular projection manifolds in Eq. (6) and (7) could be elaborated further to aid exact reproducibility.

The multi-batch scaling strategy (Appendix A.4) updates the triplane iteratively via Image Cross-Attention, but the paper does not quantify potential drift or artifact accumulation over very long trajectories.

strengths: Addresses an ambitious and practically valuable problem: generating multiview-consistent 360-degree ground-level panoramic sequences directly from a single overhead satellite image without relying on dense height maps or multiple satellite viewpoints.

Sound and elegant geometric formulation: the derivation and adaptation of epipolar constraints for equirectangular projection panoramas significantly reduces temporal attention computational complexity while enforcing multi-frame physical consistency.

The ray-based pixel attention module effectively bridges the viewpoint discrepancy between the 2D/3D triplane representation derived from the satellite image and the ground-level camera rays using deformable offsets.
Significant dataset contribution through VIGOR++, introducing over 90,000 paired satellite and continuous panoramic street-view sequences across ten metropolitan areas with ground-truth trajectories.

Thorough experimental evaluation covering single-frame quality, multi-frame consistency (FVD, CLIPSIM), 3D reconstruction fidelity (via feed-forward 3D reconstruction), comprehensive ablations, and demonstrated utility in downstream cross-view geo-localization.
weaknesses: The output resolution is limited to 128 x 512, which, while standard for cross-view evaluation benchmarks like CVUSA/VIGOR, remains relatively low for practical high-resolution panorama inspection and simulation.

As acknowledged by the authors, the model struggles when consecutive query poses are very close (< 8m), producing nearly identical outputs due to training trajectory sparsity and spatial triplane resolution limits.

The mechanism for dynamically predicting sampling offsets along the rays during diffusion denoising is briefly described in the main text and would benefit from clearer structural diagrams or pseudo-code in the main method section.

strengths: The paper addresses a significant and challenging problem: synthesizing continuous, multi-view consistent 360-degree ground-level panoramas from a single overhead satellite image and a trajectory.

The technical design is well-grounded in multi-view geometry. Extending epipolar attention to equirectangular panoramic projections provides an effective and computationally efficient way to enforce cross-frame consistency.

The ray-based pixel attention module effectively connects the 2D panoramic image plane with 3D space by sampling features along projection rays within a triplane representation, avoiding the vertical collapse inherent in pure BEV representations.
The introduction of the VIGOR++ dataset provides a valuable new benchmark for sequential satellite-to-ground synthesis, covering multiple cities with ground-truth trajectories.

The empirical evaluation is thorough, including standard image fidelity metrics, multi-view consistency metrics (FVD, CLIPSIM), 3D reconstruction consistency (3DPS/3DSS), downstream localization utility, and clear ablations for all major proposed components.
weaknesses: The generation resolution is relatively low (128x512 for full equirectangular panoramas), which limits the visual fidelity and fine structural details required for photorealistic immersive applications.

Initializing vertical planes of the triplane from a single top-down satellite image is inherently ill-posed and heavily reliant on learned hallucination; more analysis or visualization of the intermediate triplane features would clarify how well vertical structures are actually encoded before ground updates.

Comparisons against other recent sequential/3D urban generation methods (such as Sat2Scene or Streetscapes) are omitted, primarily justified by the lack of public code or differences in input assumptions, which slightly narrows the competitive baseline landscape.

The framework exhibits sensitivity to trajectory sampling density; as noted in the limitations, poses spaced less than 8 meters apart can yield redundant or nearly identical outputs due to training data sparsity and triplane resolution limits.
